Recommendation: discharge today on high‑dose oral amoxicillin to complete a 5‑day total is guideline‑concordant and appropriate.  
Rationale: she meets IDSA/ATS clinical stability criteria (afebrile >48 hours, HR <100, RR 18, hemodynamically stable, O2 requirement down to 1 L with brief room‑air tolerance, WBC normalized) and sputum grew pan‑sensitive Streptococcus pneumoniae.  
Do not extend IV or broad‑spectrum therapy beyond five days for an uncomplicated, improving CAP — narrowing to and completing oral amoxicillin was appropriate and further prolongation would be contrary to protocol.  
Before discharge, arrange outpatient follow‑up within 48–72 hours, ensure clear return precautions (worsening dyspnea, recurrent fever, altered mentation), and confirm home oxygen/pulse‑ox logistics if she will continue to use 1 L at home.  
If she cannot maintain SpO2 ≥92% on room air or develops new/worsening findings, inpatient reassessment and consideration of extended/broader therapy are required.
